:::{#exm-aft}
#### An acceleration factor of 4

Suppose the baseline survival function is exponential with mean 40 weeks,
$\surv_0(t) = \expf{-t/40}$,
and a covariate pattern $\vx$ has acceleration factor $\hazfactor(\vx) = 4$.
By @eq-aft-surv,
the probability that a subject with covariates $\vx$ is still event-free at 10 weeks is:

$$
\ba
\surv(10 \mid \vx)
&= \surv_0(10 \cdot 4)
&& \text{(AFT survival function with } t = 10 \text{ and } \hazfactor(\vx) = 4 \text{)} \\
&= \surv_0(40)
&& \text{(multiply)} \\
&= \expf{-40/40}
&& \text{(substitute the baseline survival function)} \\
&= \expf{-1}
&& \text{(divide)} \\
&\approx 0.368
&& \text{(evaluate)}
\ea
$$

A subject with covariates $\vx$ has the same chance of lasting 10 weeks
that a baseline subject has of lasting 40 weeks.

:::
